keys.text: who is on the team: each person's email maps to the 2 to 4 capital letters their ticket ids and the dashboard show; ids already in use are kept valid as legacy_ids
how new ticket ids are made: a pattern built from {type}, {initials} and {n}, or the tracker's own ids; ids already in use are kept valid as legacy_ids
which roles the team runs: ba and dev are always there, and designer adds the designer skill and its prototype gate
which coding tools accord writes skills for: claude, codex, cursor or copilot; cursor and copilot read the folders the first two write, so the default of claude and codex already serves all four

how the team merges pull requests (git.merge: merge, squash or rebase), which sets how a ticket branch takes the default branch in; nothing breaks for merge and squash, and under rebase a ticket's branch is rebased and force-pushed with a lease at verify; git.sync names a script the repository declares for that step, and nothing runs until the person runs accord trust

the name shape of a new ticket branch: {id} once, and optionally {type} (the ticket's change: word, one of branch_types) and {slug} (the title in kebab-case), as in {type}/{id}-{slug}; it applies to new branches, and an in-flight branch with the old name stops being found once the new value reaches the default branch, so change the fixed text between tickets; a later title edit, or a change: edit to another listed word, never loses the branch

the words {type} may take in the branch template, each a lower-case word such as fix; the default is feat, fix, refactor, perf, docs, test, build, ci, chore, revert and hotfix; a branch is found only by a word on this list, so removing a word while a ticket's branch carries it stops that branch being found, and a word is best removed between tickets
the most characters {slug} takes from the ticket title, a whole number from 1 to 99; the default is 40

the wording of every commit accord writes (commits.subjects), the rule a commit message must pass (commits.message) and whether trailers are allowed (commits.trailers); tickets in flight keep working because the old wording is kept as commits.legacy_subjects; commits.message.command is a script the repository declares, and nothing runs until the person runs accord trust

how a ticket's pull request title and body are made: pr.template names the template file, and pr.command is a script the repository declares that builds them, which runs only after the person runs accord trust
what happens to the pull request that only queues an idea as a draft ticket: queue.merge owner leaves it for the owner to merge, at-once merges it as soon as it opens

the JUnit report accord reads as test evidence (tests.report) and the commands the skills name for the affected and the full test run (tests.affected, tests.full); accord itself never runs a test command

how the build stage works: build.parallel is how many tasks may run at once, and build.regenerate is a script the repository declares that rebuilds generated files after a merge, which runs only after the person runs accord trust
the commands that prepare a new ticket worktree, such as installing dependencies; they run when accord opens a worktree
paths of generated files: a change there is not counted as out-of-scope work, and the security and slop checks do not read its content
names of files and folders, such as node_modules, that a finished ticket's worktree may still hold, so accord worktree clean can remove them with it
how a ticket is approved at verify: mode human means a person ticks the verification by hand, and mode outcome means accord asks the owner one approve-or-not-yet question after its report
which model and effort each accord agent uses (scout, critic, planner, executor, reviewer and the others); an agent with no entry uses its own default
from which fix round a fix executor is dispatched one model tier above the configured one (escalation.fix_round_tier_up, default 4)

how strict the gates are: strictness.rounds sets the round caps of the approach, plan and review stages, strictness.levels turns a gate or lint rule to a warning or off within the floor accord keeps, and strictness.stages switches a stage on or off
the slop check on a ticket's diff: slop.max_file_lines is the length past which a file that grew is a slop hit (default 500)
paths listed per area, such as interface or auth: a request that touches one cannot stay in lane S and is lifted to lane M, where it gets the full stages
build for a project being built, with epics and the stricter gates, or maintain for a delivered project that takes single tickets; it decides how strict the gates are

the tracker accord status reads, for display only (none, github-issues, jira, linear or script); nothing else reads it; tracker.command under the script adapter is a script the repository declares, and nothing runs until the person runs accord trust
where the design tokens live (design.tokens, a path), which a prototype may use and the linter checks it against; empty means none
how many days a claimed ticket may sit with no activity before accord audit names it as idle (default 14)
how many days an unclaimed draft ticket may sit untouched before accord audit names it as an old draft (default 90)
audit.command is a script the repository declares that adds the team's own checks to accord audit, and nothing runs until the person runs accord trust
the sections of a ticket: template.sections adds the team's own sections after accord's required ones, and a section may not replace a required one
the rule a ticket title follows: titles.rule is the team's own sentence, titles.max_length the longest title in characters, and titles.language english or any
the exact accord version this repository is pinned to; accord upgrade moves it, and every command refuses to run on a different version
ticket ids that no longer follow the id convention but stay valid; accord appends to it when a change to ids or people would strand one, and never removes from it
